learning_outcomes.text: Students know the most important concepts of imperative and object-oriented programming.
Students can design and implement their own programs.
Students can work with basic computer science concepts such as correctness, runtime, Boolean algebra, invariants, and abstract data types.
Students are able to use simple data structures (arrays, dictionaries) purposefully and know standard algorithms for them, especially for sorting arrays.

syllabus_topics: Imperative programming (variables, control structures, functions and recursion, error handling, event handling)
Introduction to a series of computer science concepts (invariants, runtime analysis, sorting algorithms, data representation in the computer, Boolean algebra)
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon passing the exam.
